name: Anomaly NIDS review
description: Intrusion detection systems (IDSs) built on artificial intelligence (AI) are presented as latent mechanisms for actively detecting fresh attacks over a complex network. Although review papers are used the systematic review or simple methods to analyse and criticize the anomaly NIDS works, the current review uses a traditional way as a quantitative description to find current gaps by synthesizing and summarizing the data comparison without considering algorithms performance. This paper presents a systematic and meta-analysis study of AI for network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) focusing on deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML) approaches in network security. Deep learning algorithms are explained in their structure, and data intrusion network is justified based on an infrastructure of networks and attack types. evaluation_method: aggregation of reported classification metrics (accuracy, F1, precision/recall, detection_rate) from reviewed studies
general_score_metric: accuracy / detection rate (primary aggregated metric reported across studies)
typical_sota_score: 90–99% (reported on legacy public IDS datasets; may be overly optimistic for real-world deployments)
reputation: This is a review/meta-analysis paper rather than a standard benchmark, so it has limited benchmark-style community adoption.
notes: Not an executable benchmark; it synthesizes prior anomaly NIDS literature and reports comparative findings rather than a single standardized score.
